subtitle: Cross-check of 12/Oct/2026, eighth day of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): Polymarket at the confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, the six post-vote national polls of 08 to 11/Oct (Datafolha, PoderData/Aya, AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, Vox Brasil, Ipespe and DataTrends), the official [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally and the press flow of 11 and 12/Oct.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 12.50% (cumulative volume USD 22.27M) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, holds steady against the confirmed reading of 11/Oct at 17:33 BRT, published in the previous update. COUNT: 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLL: 44% to 50% in DataTrends of 11/Oct; ahead only in Vox Brasil of 09/Oct, 44.2% to 42.7%.
fortes: He leads Vox Brasil of 09/Oct by 44.2% to 42.7%, within the margin of 2.15 points, and has 50.86% of the valid votes.
In AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 50.4% of Augusto Cury's voters vote for him and 38.9% for Flávio Bolsonaro; in PoderData/Aya and in Ipespe, most of them go to Flávio Bolsonaro.
🏆 Counting the closed contracts, his contract is still the one with the highest cumulative volume in the presidential book, USD 22.27M.
fracos: He stands at 12.50% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, and Flávio Bolsonaro's gap over him is 74.55pp.

He trails in five of the six national polls conducted after the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) vote: 44% to 50% in DataTrends of 11/Oct, 44% to 49% in Ipespe of 10/Oct, 45.7% to 51.1% in AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 45% to 49% in Datafolha and 44% to 49% in PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct.
He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) 1.87 points behind Flávio Bolsonaro, with 45.16% of the valid votes against 47.03%.
In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 03/Oct government approval went from 46% to 44%, with 49% disapproval.
candidates.analise: Lula stands at 12.50% in the winner contract (cumulative volume USD 22.27M), confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, and holds steady against the confirmed reading of 11/Oct at 17:33 BRT, published in the previous update. 🗳️ He had 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). 📊 In DataTrends of 11/Oct he has 44% against 50%, and his government is disapproved by 53% and approved by 45%. On 10/Oct, Ipespe gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 44%; on 09/Oct, AtlasIntel gave him 51.1% to 45.7% and Vox Brasil gave Lula 44.2% to 42.7%; on 08/Oct, Datafolha gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 45% and PoderData/Aya 49% to 44%. On 12/Oct, Lula attended Mass at the chapel of the Palácio da Alvorada and said the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) president cannot take sides (Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo); the Senate scheduled for 14/Oct the vote on the constitutional amendment (PEC) to end the 6x1 work schedule, six days on and one off (CNN Brasil and Jovem Pan). ⚖️ On 11/Oct, the TSE president, Kassio Nunes Marques, at the request of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, suspended the "Exército do Lula" channel on WhatsApp, and the inspector general (Corregedor-Geral) of the Electoral Justice, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, reinstated the channel that same afternoon. On 12/Oct, the TSE's advisory office for combating disinformation said in a report that it had not found on the channel, from 02 to 11/Oct, the false posts cited by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, but flagged risk from polarizing language and deleted messages, and Kassio summoned both campaigns to a meeting on 13/Oct (Estadão, Valor and UOL). Also on 11/Oct, Justice André Mendonça banned paid ads by Lula's campaign saying that Flávio Bolsonaro opposes ending the 6x1 schedule (UOL and Acesse Política). ⛔ The panel does not attribute the price to the polls or to the schedule: it measures the sides with each one's timestamp.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 87.05% (cumulative volume USD 19.63M) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, up 0.40pp against the confirmed reading of 11/Oct at 17:33 BRT, published in the previous update. COUNT: 47.03% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLL: 50% to 44% in DataTrends of 11/Oct; ahead in five of the six post-vote national polls.
fortes: He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) ahead, with 47.03% of the valid votes against Lula's 45.16%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally.
He stands at 87.05% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT.

He leads five of the six national polls conducted after the vote: 50% to 44% in DataTrends of 11/Oct, 49% to 44% in Ipespe of 10/Oct, 51.1% to 45.7% in AtlasIntel of 09/Oct, 49% to 45% in Datafolha and 49% to 44% in PoderData/Aya of 08/Oct; in PoderData/Aya, 54% think he will win the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno).
He has the declared support of Podemos, Augusto Cury, Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer.
Among Ronaldo Caiado's voters, he has 56% against 15% in Ipespe, 54.9% against 26.9% in AtlasIntel and 57% against 19% in PoderData/Aya.
fracos: He trails in Vox Brasil of 09/Oct, with 42.7% against 44.2%, within the margin, and in Ipespe of 10/Oct 46% say they would not vote for him under any circumstances.

🏦 According to O Globo, the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) is investigating, in the inquiry into Daniel Vorcaro and Master's relationship with BRB, the bank's R$ 3.1 million financing to Flávio Bolsonaro for the purchase of a R$ 6 million mansion in Brasília; he says the transaction was legal, and the report comes from a single media group and is included here with attribution.

📰 Messages extracted from Daniel Vorcaro's phone and published by Estadão on 24/Sep show four attempts by him to contact the banker between 13 and 16 November 2025, in the days before Vorcaro's arrest, on 17 November 2025. Gazeta do Povo confirmed the authenticity of the exchanges with its own sources close to the investigation.
candidates.analise: Flávio Bolsonaro stands at 87.05% in the winner contract (cumulative volume USD 19.63M), confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, and rises 0.40pp against the confirmed reading of 11/Oct at 17:33 BRT, published in the previous update. 🗳️ He had 47.03% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). 📊 The most recent national poll is DataTrends of 11/Oct: with 2,000 automated phone interviews from 07 to 09/Oct, Flávio Bolsonaro has 50% and Lula 44%, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 1% who don't know or didn't answer; in valid votes, 53.1% to 46.9% (Diário de São Paulo, GP1 and Poder360). On 10/Oct, Ipespe gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 44%; on 09/Oct, AtlasIntel gave him 51.1% to 45.7% and Vox Brasil gave Lula 44.2% to 42.7%; on 08/Oct, Datafolha gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 45% and PoderData/Aya 49% to 44%. 🤝 Flávio Bolsonaro has the declared support of Podemos and Augusto Cury, since 08/Oct, and of Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer; PSDB stayed neutral and released its members (Congresso em Foco and CartaCapital). Lula has the support of UP, PSTU and PCB (CNN Brasil and G1), and Renan Santos still backs no one (CNN Brasil and Estadão). On the 12/Oct holiday, Flávio Bolsonaro attended the Mass of Nossa Senhora Aparecida at the Brasília Cathedral and said he will visit his father, Jair Bolsonaro, on 13/Oct, after Alexandre de Moraes on Monday authorized the resumption of the visits, suspended since July, while barring the release of statements by the former president for political-electoral purposes (G1 and BBC News Brasil). ⚖️ On 11/Oct, the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) president, Kassio Nunes Marques, at the request of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, suspended the "Exército do Lula" channel on WhatsApp, and the inspector general (Corregedor-Geral) of the Electoral Justice, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, reinstated the channel that same afternoon. On 12/Oct, the TSE's advisory office for combating disinformation said in a report that it had not found on the channel, from 02 to 11/Oct, the false posts cited by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, but flagged risk from polarizing language and deleted messages, and Kassio summoned both campaigns to a meeting on 13/Oct (Estadão, Valor and UOL). Also on 11/Oct, Justice André Mendonça banned paid ads by Lula's campaign saying that Flávio Bolsonaro opposes ending the 6x1 work schedule, six days on and one off (UOL and Acesse Política). ⛔ The panel does not attribute the price to the polls or to the endorsements: it measures the sides with each one's timestamp.

candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): third place, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 08/Oct (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).
fortes: He finished third, with 2.89% of the valid votes, ahead of Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado.
The [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno)'s third-place book was resolved in his favour.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid more for Renan Santos, 47.50%, and for Ronaldo Caiado, 30.00%, than for him, 23.70%.
candidates.analise: Augusto Cury finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in third, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. The first round's third-place book, which on the eve paid 23.70% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, was resolved in his favour. 🤝 On 08/Oct he declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): fourth place, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): he backs neither of the two.
fortes: He finished fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes, ahead of Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18%.
His contract in the winner book closed with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, and third place went to Augusto Cury.
candidates.analise: Renan Santos finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book, behind Lula's. On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, and it was resolved in favour of Augusto Cury. 🤝 On the night of 04/Oct he said he backs neither of the two in the second round and freed Missão's activists to choose (Gazeta do Povo and Agência Brasil).

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema, with 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad did not run for President. PRICE: the three winner contracts were closed and resolved at zero.
candidates.subtitle: The three names outside the leading pack, with the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally (100% of polling sections) and the closing of the winner contracts after the first round.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 2.18% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.82M cumulative.
caiado.fortes: He declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct, with governor Daniel Vilela (O Globo and VEJA).
caiado.fracos: He finished fifth, behind Renan Santos, and the PSD decided on neutrality in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
haddad.fortes: The top of his series in the winner contract was 7.60%, on 26/May, measured in the database backup.
haddad.fracos: He was not measured by any national poll in a presidential scenario or in a second-round pairing.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 0.27% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
zema.fortes: ⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of his voters would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), the largest transfer among the names measured (O Globo).
zema.fracos: He had 0.27% of the valid votes. He declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on 05/Oct, and Novo declared support for him on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).

candidates.analise: 🗳️ Ronaldo Caiado finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fifth, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema had 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad ran for governor of São Paulo, not for President. The three contracts in the winner book were closed by Polymarket and resolved at zero. 🤝 Romeu Zema declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on the night of 05/Oct (G1 and Folha de S.Paulo), and Novo, his party, declared support on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital). Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), even with the PSD neutral in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).
fortes: Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), and Romeu Zema declared his vote for him on 05/Oct, followed by Novo on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).
⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of Romeu Zema's voters and 42% of Ronaldo Caiado's would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (O Globo).
fracos: The two are out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and the winner contracts of all three names were resolved at zero.
Fernando Haddad did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno).

cruzamento: Eighth day of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), with no new national poll on the holiday and six conducted after the vote. 💹 In the confirmed reading of 12/Oct, 15:00 BRT, Flávio Bolsonaro rises 0.40pp and Lula holds steady against the confirmed reading of 11/Oct at 17:33 BRT, published in the previous update, and the gap goes from 74.15pp to 74.55pp. 📊 The most recent national poll is DataTrends of 11/Oct: with 2,000 automated phone interviews from 07 to 09/Oct, Flávio Bolsonaro has 50% and Lula 44%, with 5% blank and spoiled ballots and 1% who don't know or didn't answer; in valid votes, 53.1% to 46.9% (Diário de São Paulo, GP1 and Poder360). On 10/Oct, Ipespe gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 44%; on 09/Oct, AtlasIntel gave him 51.1% to 45.7% and Vox Brasil gave Lula 44.2% to 42.7%; on 08/Oct, Datafolha gave Flávio Bolsonaro 49% to 45% and PoderData/Aya 49% to 44%. Of the six national polls conducted after the vote, five put Flávio Bolsonaro ahead, by 4 to 6 points, and Vox Brasil puts Lula ahead by 1.5 points. On the night of 11/Oct, PoderData/Aya released the win-expectation breakdown from its 05 to 07/Oct wave: 54% think Flávio Bolsonaro will win the second round and 37% that Lula will win; in the 03/Oct wave, on the eve of the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), the figures were 45% and 48% (CNN Brasil and Rádio Itatiaia). The voters of Augusto Cury, who declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 08/Oct, go to him by 56% to 27% in PoderData/Aya and by 50% to 29% in Ipespe, and to Lula by 50.4% to 38.9% in AtlasIntel. Among Ronaldo Caiado's voters, all three point to Flávio Bolsonaro. 🤝 Flávio Bolsonaro has the declared support of Podemos and Augusto Cury, since 08/Oct, and of Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer; PSDB stayed neutral and released its members (Congresso em Foco and CartaCapital). Lula has the support of UP, PSTU and PCB (CNN Brasil and G1), and Renan Santos still backs no one (CNN Brasil and Estadão). ⚖️ On 11/Oct, the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) president, Kassio Nunes Marques, at the request of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, suspended the "Exército do Lula" channel on WhatsApp, and the inspector general (Corregedor-Geral) of the Electoral Justice, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, reinstated the channel that same afternoon. On 12/Oct, the TSE's advisory office for combating disinformation said in a report that it had not found on the channel, from 02 to 11/Oct, the false posts cited by Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, but flagged risk from polarizing language and deleted messages, and Kassio summoned both campaigns to a meeting on 13/Oct (Estadão, Valor and UOL). Also on 11/Oct, Justice André Mendonça banned paid ads by Lula's campaign saying that Flávio Bolsonaro opposes ending the 6x1 work schedule, six days on and one off (UOL and Acesse Política). 🎙️ Record cancelled the 11/Oct debate, citing scheduling conflicts, and the second round has three debates scheduled: 15/Oct (SBT, RedeTV! and CNN Brasil), 18/Oct (Band) and 23/Oct (Globo), plus interviews with both candidates on Globo (Gazeta do Povo and Poder360). 📊 The week has 15 national polls registered with the TSE, the first full wave of the second round: 13/Oct (PoderData, Gerp, Nexus and 100 Cidades), 14/Oct ([Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest)), 15/Oct (Datafolha, AtlasIntel, Palver and Indexa) and 16/Oct (PoderData, Vox Brasil, MDA, 100 Cidades and Datavero). ⛔ The panel does not attribute price moves to the polls, the endorsements or the day's acts: it measures the sides with each one's timestamps.
